# Local file-drop feedback — 2026-10-11

Original language: English.

This records an **unreleased working-tree fix** after public 0.6.0. The isolated
development XPI still uses source version 0.6.0. The published version, tag and
package were not changed. A future publication requires a higher version and
the full [release procedure](../releases.md).

## Reproduction and behavior

The workspace's attachment hint covered and blurred the whole page. A literature
paper handled its own PDF drop and stopped propagation; the workspace's bubbling
drop handler never cleared the hint. Native reproduction with the previous build
completed PDF verification and attachment, while the overlay remained. The new
regression failed because composer feedback remained visible over a paper target.

The hint now stays inside the composer card, with an opaque shared background,
dashed border and an explicit instruction to drop inside that box. Drags over
the surrounding workspace can reveal it; only a drop within the card prepares
a chat attachment. Drops elsewhere are prevented from navigating the workspace
and add no attachment.

Review overlays suppress composer feedback. Each paper's PDF target handles file
enter/over events and sets the copy effect itself. A document capture listener
clears composer feedback even when a nested target handles the drop. Escape,
drag end, leaving the workspace and window blur also clear it. Workspace disposal
removes the listeners. Feedback stays pointer-transparent and does not change
the draft or acquire keyboard focus.

## Validation

- `npm test`: 1,354 tests passed, with no failures, skips or cancellations.
- `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` and
  `npm run build --workspace @confucius/zotero-addon` passed.
- `CONFUCIUS_LITERATURE_OUTPUT=output/file-drop-live node --import tsx scripts/live-literature.mjs`:
  **37 native check groups** passed, with no UI errors.

The drag checks cover moving from the workspace into a paper target, highlighting
only that target, completing the actual verified PDF attachment and clearing
feedback without calling chat attachment preparation. Composer checks cover
bounded geometry, no backdrop blur, pointer transparency, rejecting outside
drops, Escape/dragend/blur/leave cleanup, a real prepared PDF attachment, preserving
the input draft and removing the prepared attachment afterward. Screenshot
checks wait for the hint's opacity transition to finish.

The remaining literature checks retain candidate confirmation/revision behavior,
PDF parsing/import and invalid-file rejection, continuation during retrieval,
late-response focus protection, restart recovery and narrow-window controls.

Environment: macOS 26.6.2 (ARM64), Zotero 10.0.6, Node.js 23.10.0, an empty
isolated profile and an ordinary installed development XPI. Drag events were
dispatched in actual Gecko; native PDF verification and attachment preparation
ran through their real implementations. OpenAlex, model and download transport
responses were deterministic fixtures. No personal library, service keys or
online models were used.

Tested XPI SHA-256:
`3f40c4919577f2973fbb5b1944da738e3d633da92dc515b129c39e12b70aff5b`.

## Interface checklist and limits

The hint uses shared palette variables, the existing composer bounds and dashed
target styling. Light/Chinese and dark/English screenshots confirm readable
feedback, including a 280px window without horizontal overflow. Paper review and
the surrounding workspace remain visible; empty/disabled handling and cleanup
passed. Artifact reader controls, spacing and decoration are unchanged. Both
language versions of the design and user guides were updated.

This run did not include manual Finder/browser OS drag gestures, Windows/Linux,
Zotero 7/8/9, OS font scaling, OS high-contrast mode, installed-package upgrades
or publication. Raw reports, screenshots and isolated profiles remain in ignored
`output/`.
